title: The Miracle Green Carpet: How We Started Our Azolla Farming Journey
excerpt: What if you could grow a highly nutritious superfood that doubles its size every few days, slashes your animal feed bills, and naturally fertilizes your crops all on a simple patch of water? Welcome to our new venture into Azolla farming!
author: Cynthia Jelagat
content:
Every farmer knows the quiet anxiety of looking at feed prices. Month after month, commercial dairy meals, poultry layers, and supplements seem to climb higher, eating away at the hard-earned profits of a working farm. For a long time, we asked ourselves a tough question: How do we cut down these heavy input costs without sacrificing the health and productivity of our livestock?

The answer didn't come from a commercial store or an expensive machinery catalog. Instead, it came in the form of a tiny, brilliant green, free-floating aquatic fern. Welcome to the beginning of our journey with Azolla.

When we first dug out our shallow ponds and lined them with plastic sheets, it felt like an ambitious science experiment. We added soil, mixed in a little organic manure, filled them with water, and introduced our first handfuls of Azolla starter culture. To be honest, we watched those ponds like hawks. But within just a few days, something incredible happened. The tiny green fronds began to multiply at a breathtaking speed, weaving together to create a thick, vibrant velvet carpet across the water.

Seeing that rapid growth confirmed what we had hoped: Azolla isn't just an easy plant to cultivate; it is an absolute game-changer for sustainable agriculture. Here is a look at the incredible benefits we are discovering as we dive deep into this miracle crop.

title: CHI Acquires Two Beehives to Support Conservation and Community Income
excerpt: Thanks to generous donations from well-wishers, Clean Heights Initiative has acquired two beehives near the Elgeyo Escarpment — a small but meaningful step towards building sustainable income for our conservation work.
author: Roy Chumba
content:
We are grateful.

Thanks to donations from well-wishers who believe in what 
we are doing here in Elgeyo Marakwet, and through the able 
leadership of Cynthia Jelagat, Clean Heights Initiative has 
acquired two beehives, now placed near the Elgeyo 
Escarpment.

The goal is straightforward. Honey production will generate 
income that goes directly back into CHI's programmes  
supporting our clean-up exercises, tree planting work and 
community activities.

Beyond income, bees play a vital role in the health of the 
escarpment ecosystem. As our hives grow, so does the 
pollination activity that supports the native vegetation we 
work so hard to protect.

This is conservation and livelihood working together — 
exactly the kind of practical, community-rooted initiative 
CHI was built around.

To everyone who contributed  thank you. Every donation, 
no matter the size, is making a real difference on the 
ground here in Iten.

Follow our progress on Instagram 
@clean_heights_initiative

title: We Are Growing a Forest: CHI's Community Tree Nursery Takes Root in Iten
excerpt: Donated by well-wishers, grown by our community, planted on the hills of Elgeyo Marakwet. This is not just reforestation  this is the highlands healing themselves.
author: Cynthia Jelagat
content:
At Clean Heights Initiative we are always looking for more ways 
to improve the environment around us. This time we decided to 
start a tree nursery.

Well-wishers and community members in Iten contributed what they 
could to make this happen. From those contributions we have started 
growing indigenous tree seedlings right here in Iten, tended by 
community members every day.

Every tree we plant comes from a local nursery. Buying from local 
growers keeps the money inside Elgeyo Marakwet and gives local 
families an income from conservation work.

The trees will be planted on degraded hillsides and along riverbanks 
across the escarpment. Over time we want the nursery to generate its 
own income so this work can sustain itself.

This is just the beginning. If you want to support the nursery 
or join a planting day, contact us at 
info@cleanheightsinitiative.org or find us on Instagram 
@clean_heights_initiative.
